rationale: Interaction-picture evolution is appropriate when a Hamiltonian has a dominant exactly or cheaply evolvable reference component.
For canonical Pauli input, OpenQEvo selects all diagonal I/Z terms as the reference by default; callers can provide reference_term_indices when a different split is justified.
The method is executable as a dense midpoint reference, so its numerical convergence should be checked by increasing steps.
warnings: This is an experimental dense reference implementation, not an interaction-picture circuit, LCU method, or asymptotic resource estimate.
The automatic diagonal reference split is heuristic; validate a caller-selected split and convergence for the problem of interest.

evidence.note: Supports the split-Hamiltonian applicability condition and the need to identify a useful reference component.

alternatives.reason: Use a circuit-oriented executable baseline when no useful reference split is available.
Use a dense small-system static-Hamiltonian reference when a direct Krylov approximation is a better numerical comparison.
